enable_ocpp.title: Switch OCPP on at the charger
enable_ocpp.description:
1. Wait for the Wi-Fi icon on the charger screen.
2. On the charger press OK, choose Wi-Fi, switch OCPP on and leave the menu.
3. Click Submit.

If the Wi-Fi icon does not appear, close this window, check the network name and password and start again.

manual_address.title: Server address for the charger
manual_address.description:
Check that the address below contains the IP address of your Home Assistant. If it shows a different address, for example ws://172.17.0.2, close this window, open Settings → System → Network, in Local network switch Automatic off, enter http://computer-IP-address:8123, click Save and start again.

In the EV-Charger app, in the OCPP settings, enter:

- server address: `{url}`
- ChargeID: `{serial}`

Then on the charger press OK, choose Wi-Fi — the address you entered is shown there — switch OCPP on and leave the menu. Click Submit.

modbus_intro.title: ModBus TCP: before you start
modbus_intro.description:
In ModBus mode Home Assistant talks to the charger directly in the local network. Prepare the charger first:

1. **Wi-Fi.** Connect the charger to Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) with the charger app over Bluetooth, with DHCP on, and reserve its IP address in the router (or set a fixed IP in the app). ModBus TCP works only over Wi-Fi. While ModBus is on, the charger cannot be set up over Bluetooth.
2. **Menu "Load & communication".** Switch load balancing on and choose the communication mode **ModBus TCP** (not RS485, not EM3-Box). OCPP and ModBus cannot work at the same time.
3. **Menu "Current adjustment".** Set it to the maximum of the charger: the charger uses the lower of this value and the limit from Home Assistant.
4. **Menu "Charge mode".** Switch Plug & charge off to start and stop from Home Assistant (it is on from the factory).
5. Switch off the charger's own reservations (they fight the Home Assistant schedule) and set the date and time on the charger.
6. Switch off the charger's "1-phase mode" if you want to switch between 1 and 3 phases.
7. **Only one ModBus program.** Switch off evcc and other integrations or devices that use ModBus of this charger.

modbus_model.title: ModBus TCP: charger {serial}
modbus_model.description:
Check the charger version; it sets the maximum current.

Stopping a charge and switching phases while charging over ModBus require firmware 3.1 or newer (the version is shown on the charger screen). On older firmware, for example 2.7, the charger does not stop on a stop command: it lowers the current to the minimum and accepts no new commands until the cable is unplugged from the car. To stop a charge on such firmware, unplug the cable from the car. For full control use the OCPP connection.

If this charger also has an OCPP entry, that entry shows "not connected" while the charger is in ModBus mode; you may disable it.

site.title: GNLT site: grid connection (beta)
site.description:
The site controls the chosen ModBus chargers together: no grid phase goes above the fuse limit, and each charger can charge from PV surplus (charge mode on its device page).

Grid meter: one current sensor per phase, in amperes, import positive and export negative. If your meter shows import as negative, turn on "Invert sign".

This function is in beta and does not replace the electrical protection (circuit breaker) of the installation.

data.grid_invert: Invert sign of the grid sensors

data_description.meter_period_s: How often the meter sensors get a new value; the site works in the same rhythm (default 10 s).
data_description.max_total_power_w: Limit of the whole connection in watts, if the contract sets one.
data_description.grid_power: Without it the grid power is calculated from the three currents x 230 V.

site_member.title: GNLT site: charger {name} (beta)
site_member.description:
Priority: 1 is served first; chargers with the same number share equally.

Grid phase of charger L1: the grid phase its L1 terminal is wired to (rotated wiring spreads single-phase cars over the phases).

site_pv.title: GNLT site: PV charging (beta)
site_pv.description: Used in the charge modes "PV" and "Min + PV". Defaults: start when the surplus covers the minimum current for 1 minute, stop when it has been missing for 3 minutes.

data_description.enable_threshold_w: 0 = automatic: the surplus must cover the minimum current. A negative value is the export needed to start.

station_not_responding.title: {name}: no connection over ModBus
station_not_responding.description:
The charger has not answered for 3 minutes. Check in this order:

1. Wait 3 minutes: after a reconnect the charger may stay silent, and after a Home Assistant crash it may still hold the previous connection.
2. No other program uses ModBus of this charger (evcc, other integrations, other devices on port 502).
3. The charger is not switched to OCPP.
4. The IP address of the charger has not changed (Wi-Fi menu of the charger).
5. In the charger menu switch ModBus TCP or load management off and on.
6. Switch the charger's mains power off for at least 10 seconds and wait about 20 seconds.

This message disappears by itself when the charger answers again.

identity_mismatch.title: {name}: another charger answers at this address
identity_mismatch.description: Another device (serial number {serial_seen}) answers at the address of this charger - the router may have given the address to another unit. Home Assistant sends no commands until this charger answers again. Reserve a fixed IP address for the charger in the router and enter it in the charger settings.

relay_welded.title: {name}: power relay stuck - service needed
relay_welded.description: The charger reports a stuck (welded) power relay. This is a safety fault: Home Assistant starts no charge while the charger reports this error. Contact the seller for service.

confirm.description: After a power cut the charger switched Plug & Charge back on. It now starts charging by itself and does not take start and stop commands from Home Assistant. Submit to switch Plug & Charge off on {name} again (your setting).

site_stopped.description: The GNLT site stopped controlling its chargers ({reason}). Every charger was left at its minimum current; the site starts or stops nothing until it runs again. Reload the site in Settings -> Devices & services; if it stops again, send its diagnostics to the seller.
